Only faith
farre foeuer the thing that is ſaid ſurmounteth our vnderſtanding For ſo heroical
was the act of Abrahams faith, promptly belieuing Gods word in a mattet moſt
hard to his former conceit, that for the ſame he receiued ſingular prayſe: and
for the Like afterwards was called The father manie Nations (c. 17. v. 5.) and by
S. Paul Ybe father of al that belieue (Ro. 4. v. 11.) whete the Apoſtle teacheth that
Abrabam had no iuſtice, nor eſtitnation of iuſtice before God, vntil he belieued
in Chriſt (v. 18. 19, 20.) becauſe al workes before that faith are inſufficient.
Neither was this a fole faith, but had other neceſſarie vertues of hope, and cha-
titie, hutnilitie, reuerence, obedience, and the like iovned with it. Wherfore
S Iames teſtificth that Abraham was iuſtified by workes ( that is by workes
following faith, not going before faith.) For Faith (faith he) if it haue not worker,
doth not iuſti-is dead iait-ſelf, (c. 2. v. 17.) And by workes Abrahams faith wat conſummate v. 22.
